 Follow Bo French loses Texas election, gets booted from country club after UT racism roil
 Rhyma Castillo Thu, November 19, 2026 at 6:15 PM UTC Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Tarrant County Republican Party Chair Bo French speaks during a rally, on Tuesday, April 15, 2025, in Mansfield. (Shafkat Anowar/Dallas Morning News) As it turns out, a seat on the Texas Railroad Commission wasn't the only thing Republican Bo French lost this November.
 The former Tarrant County GOP chairman has been booted from one of Fort Worth's oldest country clubs following a controversy over his social media remarks, which drew bipartisan accusations of racism from both Democrats and fellow Republicans.
 In a Nov. 10 letter obtained by Politico , River Crest Country Club notified French that its board of directors had voted to immediately revoke his membership "for reasons relating to the reputation and general welfare of the Club."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement According to French, the ordeal had been brewing for months. In a Wednesday post on X, the Republican said the board had asked him to voluntarily relinquish his membership in September over "racist posts." He refused, prompting the board to convene an expulsion hearing.
 ALSO READ: Nine islands, two countries: Texas' land grab claim faces new scrutiny
 "Nothing I said in September was racist," French said in a statement he read to the board.
 On Sept. 13, French shared a photo of predominantly South Asian students cheering at a Longhorns football game, writing: "I heard UT graduation this year looked like this. I didn't believe it. The problem is now obviously far worse than anyone imagined." In another post, he lamented "how many Americans have been displaced by foreigners."
 Advertisement Advertisement Despite bipartisan criticism, French defended his remarks, arguing that the university's admissions and hiring practices disadvantaged Texans.
 Established in 1911, River Crest touts itself as a "who's who" of Fort Worth, with a sprawling, 6,368-yard golf course. The club declined to discuss French's expulsion with Politico, citing its policy regarding "past, present and prospective members." It did not immediately respond to a request for comment from the Express-News.
 The decision capped off a particularly rough week for French, whose campaign for a spot on the state commission overseeing Texas' oil and gas industry ended in a defeat by Democrat Jon Rosenthal by roughly 677,000 votes.
